text:
maria: Heads up — since ~08:10 UTC we've been seeing a controller-manager reconcile flood in eu-south1 that's blocking GPU pool claims. Graphs show pendingReconciles spiking from ~200 -> 6k in 2m. apiserver 503s follow shortly after.

sam: ack, seeing it on our side too. kube-controller-manager CPU at 95% on the leader pod. pod restarts starting at 08:12.

leo: any recent kube upgrades or config changes?

maria: no planned changes. Last deploy was 3h ago (model-serving infra). ops-bot: detected controller-manager leader-election change 3x in 4m (timestamps: 1746654330, 1746654346, 1746654362).

anya: leader flapping would explain a reconcile pileup. when the leader steps down controllers requeue objects. what objects are hot?

maria: mostly our GPUPool CRs and NodeClaims. Lots of requeues for nodes with DeletionTimestamp mismatch. logs: ```W0510 08:11:02.345 controller.go:92] object "gpu-pool/eu-south-gpu-1" requeued: reconcile took too long```

diego: noticed conntrack on the kube-proxy host creeping up. SNAT table near 64k. We had a NAT rebalance in that region last week. could be related.

jun: if apiserver calls are failing intermittently, controller-manager leader checks (list/watch) might be timing out and triggering new elections. apiserver logs show `etcd: request timed out` around the same time.

sam: quick mitigation idea — reduce reconcile bursts by bumping leader-election lease to 30s and increase client QPS burst for controller manager? risky but can reduce churn.

anya: agree for short term. also throttle GPUPool reconciler if possible (rate limiter). can we patch a canary?

maria: created a rollback patch to bump leaseDuration from 15s -> 30s on the staging controller-manager config. deploying to eu-south staging now. deploy-bot: rollout started for `ctrlmgr-config/eu-south` -> canary.

diego: meanwhile I'm nuking stale conntrack entries on two NAT boxes to free up table. will monitor SNAT count.

leo: question — are GPU attach timeouts exacerbating this? I've seen attach calls hang for 60s then time out and requeue node claims.

maria: yes, attach latency spiked to 3x baseline. cause appears to be NVMe attach backend taking longer under load. adding that to the incident blamemap.

jun: checking etcd metrics — leader e2e latency increased at 08:09, followers falling behind. suspect intermittent IO stall on the etcd leader disk. we saw one slow wal commit there.

sam: summary of actions: 1) canary lease bump in staging (maria) 2) conntrack prune (diego) 3) increase ctrlmgr QPS/burst in canary (maria) 4) SSH to etcd leader disk checks (jun).

anya: what's the customer impact? are active jobs failing?

maria: some provisioning requests are queued; a handful of inference pods reported delayed GPU assignment (~+2m). no large-scale 503 outage yet but SLOs degraded.

diego: conntrack prune freed ~4k entries, SNAT headroom back to safe. after prune we saw fewer apiserver 5xx for ~30s.

ops-bot: canary leaseDuration change applied to staging at 1746654352. Monitoring for election rate and pendingReconciles.

maria: canary looks promising — leader election stabilized and pendingReconciles dropped to ~350 after 40s. staging attach latency also decreased slightly.

jun: still seeing some etcd wal latency spikes; ops, can we verify IO for leader instance? cc @infra-team.

leo: propose longer-term fixes: - increase etcd leader IOPS (move to provisioned NVMe) - add backpressure in GPUPool reconciler - tighten NAT rebalance automation so conntrack doesn't spike during rolling updates - better observability: correlate attach RPC latencies with leader-election events.

sam: agree. also documenting runbook steps we used here. I'll open a follow-up PR for rate-limiter defaults.

maria: thanks team. I'll escalate to infra for disk IOPS and schedule a postmortem once we confirm root cause. :thumbsup:

diego: marking this thread resolved for now, will reopen if we see >50% reclaim failures in the next hour.

deploy-bot: canary -> promoted to eu-south config at 1746654375 (no regressions observed).

maria: closing — keep an eye on the dashboards and add any anomalies to the PM.
